content: 1. Zumab reduces the levels of ethinylestradiol by influencing the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. 2. Nemolizumab suppresses cytokines, potentially increasing CYP enzyme activity. Monitor for reduced systemic levels of narrow therapeutic or sensitive CYP substrates affected by CYP inducers after initiating nemolizumab. Dosage modifications may be necessary. 3. Neomycin (oral) decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by influencing the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Nirmatrelvir decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by increasing its metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. Consider using an additional nonhormonal contraceptive method for the remainder of the cycle. The mechanism is unknown but may involve ritonavir-induced CYP2C9 or CYP1A2 induction. 7. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by increasing its metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. Consider using an additional nonhormonal contraceptive method for the remainder of the cycle. The mechanism is unknown but may involve ritonavir-induced CYP2C9 or CYP1A2 induction. 8. Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Ofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of olanzapine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Oteseconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol through mechanisms involving BCRP inhibition. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. Oteseconazole, as a BCRP inhibitor, may enhance the effects and risks of toxicities of BCRP substrates. Use the lowest starting dose of the BCRP substrate or consider reducing its dose. 12. Paromomycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Penicillin G aqueous decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as there is a risk of oral contraceptive failure. 14. Penicillin VK decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Pioglitazone decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by influencing the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of rasagiline by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2. Use caution and monitor closely, especially when using 5 mg daily in combination with CYP1A2 inhibitors. 20. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by influencing the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Romidepsin decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol through receptor-binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of ropinirole by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2. The interaction mechanism is unspecified. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by influencing the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 24. Rufinamide decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Rufinamide is a weak inducer of CYP3A4 and can reduce the exposure of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates. 25. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of selegiline (oral and transdermal) by inhibiting its N-demethylation. Use caution and monitor closely.
